info.title: NeView — MongoDB API
info.description:
Reviews, awards, popularity and user management REST API served by the **Express.js / MongoDB** backend.

Includes:
- Rotten Tomatoes-style review CRUD
- Oscar nominations and wins (filterable, grouped by film)
- Redis-backed popularity rankings (today, this week, trending, …)
- Like toggle and view tracking (synced to PostgreSQL via BullMQ)
- JWT-based user registration, login, and profile

Protected endpoints require `Authorization: Bearer <token>` (obtain from `POST /api/user/login`).

Oscar winners that also received at least one Rotten review on the platform,

Cached for **1 hour**.

post.summary: Toggle like / unlike for a movie 🔒
post.description:
Toggles the authenticated user's like for a movie.

- If the user has **not** liked the movie → creates a like document, returns `liked: true`.
- If the user has **already** liked the movie → removes the like, returns `liked: false`.

After a successful write:
1. A 5-second per-user-per-movie Redis cooldown is set.
2. A BullMQ event is published to sync the count to PostgreSQL asynchronously.
3. The Redis popularity counter is incremented (likes only, not unlikes).

Rate limits: **20 requests/minute** (Express-rate-limit) + **5-second cooldown** (Redis).

message.example: Please wait before toggling your like.

post.summary: Sync a movie title into the local cache
post.description:
Internal service-to-service endpoint. Adds a movie title to the
in-memory/Redis movie title cache used for search autocomplete.

Requires a static bearer token passed as `Authorization: Bearer <INTERNAL_TOKEN>`
(configured via the `INTERNAL_TOKEN` environment variable — **not** a user JWT).

Submits a new Fresh or Rotten review for a movie.
Requires a valid JWT. Rate-limited to **5 submissions per 15 minutes** per user.

After saving, the Redis stats cache for the movie is updated atomically
(no cache invalidation needed).

Tracks a page view for popularity scoring. Public — no authentication
required. Rate-limited to **30 requests/minute per IP**.

Returns `202 Accepted` immediately; the Redis write is fire-and-forget
so a slow Redis instance never blocks the page load.

get.description:
Returns pre-computed Rotten Tomatoes-style statistics for a single movie.
Cached in Redis for **24 hours**.

`tomatometer` is `null` (not `0`) when a movie has no reviews, so the
frontend can distinguish "unrated" from "0% rotten".

post.description:
Verifies the supplied credentials using Argon2id and returns a signed JWT.
The error message is intentionally vague ("Invalid email or password") to
prevent user enumeration.

get.description: Returns version info and available endpoint paths.

Returns Oscar records grouped by film, with all nominations and wins
for each film collected into an `awards` array.

**Filters** (all optional, combinable):
- `year_ceremony` — exact ceremony year (1929 – present)
- `category` — award category name
- `winner` — `true` | `false`
- `from_date` / `to_date` — film release year range

**Sort** (`sortBy`): comma-separated `field-direction` pairs.
Allowed fields: `winsCount`, `totalNominations`, `year_film`, `film`.

Results are cached in Redis.

parameters.name: year_ceremony
parameters.description: Filter by ceremony year (e.g. `2020` for the 92nd Academy Awards).

post.description:
Creates a new user account. The password is hashed with **Argon2id** via
a pre-save hook — the plain-text password is never stored.

On success, a JWT is issued immediately so the user is logged in right away.

400.description: Missing fields or password too short.
